worked_exemplar.historical_question: As of 2024-12-01, will the monthly retail diesel-price change for United States diesel price in 2024-12 be at least -1.941 percent?
worked_exemplar.target_semantics: The monthly percentage change in US retail diesel prices for December 2024 must be greater than or equal to -1.941%.
expert_reasoning: The core of the prediction relies on calculating the monthly percentage change in US retail diesel prices for December 2024.
This calculation requires two key inputs: the US retail diesel price in November 2024 and the US retail diesel price in December 2024.
The target condition is met if this calculated percentage change is at least -1.941%.
worked_exemplar.counterevidence: No forecast-time evidence was provided to support or contradict any of the causal links or factors influencing the diesel price change.
worked_exemplar.prospective_target_estimate: The provided DAG structure indicates that the target is a binary outcome ('yes' or 'no') based on a price change threshold. Without any forecast-time evidence, a specific estimate cannot be made, and the outcome remains uncertain.
worked_exemplar.option_mapping: The 'yes' option corresponds to the monthly retail diesel-price change being greater than or equal to -1.941 percent. The 'no' option corresponds to the monthly retail diesel-price change being less than -1.941 percent.
worked_exemplar.uncertainty: The absence of any forecast-time evidence means that the predictive power of the identified drivers and mediators cannot be assessed. All causal links remain unsupported and their current relevance unknown, leading to high uncertainty.
worked_exemplar.dag_derived_lesson: When evaluating a target metric that is a calculated value, it is crucial to have evidence supporting the inputs to that calculation and the calculation mechanism itself. A threshold comparison requires evidence that not only supports the direction of change but also the magnitude relative to the specified boundary.
